title: ukbflow
text: 📚 文档 • 🚀 快速开始 • 🎨 Tessera • 🧪 Palette Lab • 💬 问题反馈 • 🤝 贡献指南 语言： English | 简体中文

title: ukbflow
text: ukbflow 的定位是面向 UK Biobank 受控数据平台的 R-native、RAP-aware 工作流系统。它为表型提取、疾病衍生、关联分析、可复现表型配方、审计记录和发表级输出提供统一的工作流层，同时让个体水平数据保留在 RAP 环境中。 UK Biobank 数据政策（2024+）：个体水平数据必须保留在 RAP 环境中，不得下载到本地。ukbflow 旨在支持符合该约束的 RAP 原生分析流程；用户仍需确保仅下载获准的汇总级结果。
code: library(ukbflow)  # 打开审计 manifest：分析过程中自动记录做了什么 aud <- audit_start("smoking_lung_cancer")  # 本地生成合成 UKB 数据（在 RAP 上请替换为 extract_batch() + job_wait()） data <- ops_toy(n = 5000, seed = 2026) |>   derive_missing()  # 衍生肺癌结局（ICD-10 C34）及随访时间 data <- data |>   derive_icd10(name = "lung", icd10 = "C34",                source = c("cancer_registry", "hes")) |>   derive_followup(name         = "lung",                   event_col    = "lung_icd10_date",                   baseline_col = "p53_i0",                   censor_date  = as.Date("2022-10-31"),                   death_col    = "p40000_i0")  # 定义暴露变量：曾吸烟 vs. 从不吸烟 data[, smoking_ever := factor(   ifelse(p20116_i0 == "Never", "Never", "Ever"),   levels = c("Never", "Ever") )]  # Cox 回归：吸烟 → 肺癌（三模型校正框架） res <- assoc_coxph(data,   outcome_col  = "lung_icd10",   time_col     = "lung_followup_years",   exposure_col = "smoking_ever",   covariates   = c("p21022", "p31", "p22189"))  # 森林图 —— 直接传入结果表，自动推导估计值 / 置信区间 / 列 / 坐标轴 plot_forest(res)  # 记录模型并写出 manifest：字段 ID、队列快照、表型摘要、 # 模型结果与 session metadata，输出为 JSON aud <- audit_model(aud, res) audit_write(aud, "smoking_lung_cancer_audit.json")

title: ukbflow
text: ukbflow 当前聚焦于 UK Biobank 表型提取流程中最常用、最稳定的疾病表型来源： GP 处方（gp_scripts）和数值测量值暂不属于当前 public API。 UKB 的死亡注册和 First Occurrence 字段没有 ICD-9 或 OPCS-4 对应版本。

title: ukbflow
text: ukbflow 是工作流系统，不替代底层 RAP 和统计工具。它围绕 dx-toolkit / DNAnexus 任务、R 建模函数、绘图包以及基于 PLINK2 的 GRS 流程进行封装、编排与记录。 它不提供通用 DAG 调度器，不估算 RAP 费用，不替代 DNAnexus 界面，也不替代研究设计、 协变量选择、表型有效性判断或因果解释。当前 public phenotype helpers 聚焦上表列出的 UKB 数据来源，含初级保健诊断（Read v2 / CTV3）；GP 处方与数值测量暂不覆盖。

title: ukbflow
text: auth_login()、auth_status()、auth_logout()、auth_list_projects()、auth_select_project() — RAP 认证 fetch_ls()、fetch_tree() — 浏览 RAP 文件系统 extract_ls()、extract_pheno()、extract_batch() — 表型提取 extract_gp() — 导出 GP 初级保健 record 表（gp_clinical 等） extract_olink() — 导出 Olink 蛋白组 entity（约 2900 个蛋白，NPX 值） extract_nmr() — 导出 249 个 Nightingale NMR 代谢物 decode_values() — 整数编码 → 可读标签 decode_names() — 字段 ID → snake_case 列名 job_status() — 按 ID 查询任务状态 job_wait() — 阻塞等待任务完成（支持超时） job_path() — 获取已完成任务的输出路径 job_result() — 获取任务结果对象 job_ls() — 列出最近提交的任务 derive_missing() — 处理”不知道”/“不愿回答” derive_covariate() — 类型转换 + 分布汇总 derive_cut() — 连续变量分组 derive_selfreport() — 自报告疾病状态 + 日期 derive_hes() — HES 住院 ICD-10 derive_hes_icd9() — HES 住院 ICD-9（少数遗留编码体系） derive_opcs() — HES 住院 OPCS-4 手术操作 derive_gp_read2() — GP 初级保健诊断（Read v2），基于自行提供的 gp_clinical 表 derive_gp_ctv3() — GP 初级保健诊断（CTV3 / Read v3） derive_first_occurrence() — First Occurrence 字段 derive_algorithm() — 算法判定结局（Category 42 判定后的日期字段） derive_cancer_registry() — 癌症注册（ICD-10） derive_cancer_registry_icd9() — 癌症注册（ICD-9） derive_death_registry() — 死亡注册 derive_icd10() — 多源 ICD-10 合并（封装函数） derive_icd9() — 多源 ICD-9 合并（封装函数） derive_case() — 自报告 + ICD-10 + 可选 ICD-9 / OPCS-4 / GP（Read v2 / CTV3）最终合并 derive_recipe() — 一次调用跑完一个内置表型配方 derive_timing() — 患病时间分类（现患 vs. 新发） derive_age() — 事件发生年龄 derive_followup() — 随访终止日期与随访年数 assoc_coxph() / assoc_cox() — Cox 比例风险模型（HR） assoc_logistic() / assoc_logit() — 逻辑回归（） assoc_linear() / assoc_lm() — 线性回归（β） assoc_coxph_zph() — 比例风险假设检验 assoc_subgroup() — 分层分析 + 交互项 LRT assoc_trend() — 剂量-反应趋势 + p_trend assoc_competing() — Fine-Gray 竞争风险（SHR） assoc_lag() — 滞后暴露敏感性分析 assoc_rcs() — 限制性立方样条剂量反应（非线性 + p-nonlinear） assoc_evalue() — 未测量混杂的 E-value 敏感性分析 plot_forest() — 森林图（PNG / PDF / JPG / TIFF，300 dpi） plot_survival() — 生存曲线（Kaplan-Meier，PNG / PDF / JPG / TIFF，300 dpi） plot_rcs() — 限制性立方样条剂量反应曲线（PNG / PDF / JPG / TIFF，300 dpi） plot_tableone() — 基线特征表（DOCX / HTML / PDF / PNG） ops_setup() — 环境健康检查（dx CLI、RAP 认证、R 包依赖） ops_fields() — 搜索当前 RAP 项目中已获批的 UKB 字段 ops_fields_common() — 离线字段速查表：手选常用字段，外加血常规、血生化、NMR 三个完整 panel ops_fo() — 1,165 个首次发生（First Occurrence）结局的离线速查表，按 3 字符 ICD-10 码给出日期与来源字段号 ops_alg() — 19 个算法判定结局（Category 42）的离线速查表，按结局给出日期与来源字段号 ops_covariates() — 常用协变量预设的离线目录，返回解码后的列名 ops_toy() — 生成合成 UKB 风格数据，用于开发与测试 ops_na() — 逐列汇总缺失值（NA 与 ""）及缺失率 ops_snapshot() — 记录流程检查点，追踪数据集在各步骤的变化 ops_snapshot_cols() — 获取指定快照保存的列名列表 ops_snapshot_diff() — 比较两个快照之间的列差异 ops_snapshot_remove() — 删除某快照之后新增的列 ops_set_safe_cols() — 设置受保护列，ops_snapshot_remove 不会删除这些列 ops_withdraw() — 从队列中排除 UKB 撤回参与者 recipe_list() — 列出内置的表型定义配方库 recipe_get() — 读取单个配方为规范化的 ukbflow_recipe 对象 recipe_sources() — 将配方规则摊平为一行一条规则的整洁表 recipe_rule() — 构建单条来源规则 recipe_new() — 构建并校验配方，无需手写 YAML recipe_write() — 将配方对象写出为 YAML 文件 print() — 以可读形式渲染配方定义 derive_recipe() — 将配方应用到数据（归在 derive_* 家族；只新增 {id}_status / {id}_date 两列） audit_start() — 创建分析审计对象，记录包版本与 session metadata audit_fields() — 记录提取所用的 UKB 字段 ID audit_snapshot() — 记录队列大小、列数、缺失列数和完整列名 audit_cols() — 从 audit snapshot 中取回列名 audit_pheno() — 基于 derive_* 标准命名汇总衍生表型 audit_recipe() — 记录版本化表型配方，内嵌自包含的定义快照 audit_model() — 记录关联分析结果表；outcome/time/协变量等调用细节从 assoc_* 自动读取 audit_job() — 记录 DNAnexus job ID，并在可用时记录轻量任务 metadata audit_write() — 将 audit manifest 写出为 JSON audit_read() — 将 JSON manifest 读回成可用的 audit 对象 audit_diff() — 对比同一个 audit 对象内的两条记录（比如快照前后列变化、模型间协变量变化），或对比两个 audit 对象的整体结构 audit_flowchart() — 从记录的快照导出队列衰减表，可直接喂给流程图渲染工具 print() / summary() — 打印简短或详细的 audit 总览 grs_check() — 验证 SNP 权重文件 grs_bgen2pgen() — 在 RAP 上将 BGEN 转换为 PGEN（提交云端任务） grs_score() — 使用 plink2 跨染色体计算 GRS grs_standardize() / grs_zscore() — Z 分标准化 grs_validate() — /HR per SD、高 vs. 低、趋势检验、AUC/C-index

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: assoc_* functions fit regression models exposure variable return tidy result tables suitable downstream forest plots publication tables. Prerequisite: analysis dataset already contain derived case status, follow-time, covariates produced derive_* functions. See vignette("derive") vignette("derive-survival").
code: library(ukbflow)  # ops_toy(scenario = "association") returns a pre-derived analysis-ready table: # covariates already as factors, bmi_cat / tdi_cat binned, and two outcomes # (dm_* and htn_*) with status / date / timing / followup columns in place. dt <- ops_toy(scenario = "association") dt <- dt[dm_timing != 1L]   # incident analysis: exclude prevalent DM cases

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: main functions automatically produce three adjustment levels without requiring manual formula construction: Age sex columns located automatically small set standard UKB ukbflow names: age_at_recruitment, p21022, 21022, participant.p21022 age, sex, p31, 31, participant.p31 sex. columns manually renamed, set base = FALSE pass intended age sex columns covariates. Set base = FALSE skip first two models run Fully adjusted model.

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: assoc_coxph() primary function time--event outcomes. accepts logical (TRUE/FALSE) integer (0/1) event indicators returns one row per exposure x term x model combination. Output columns: n, n_events, person_years reflect model-specific complete-case analysis set — participants missing value across outcome, time, exposure, covariates dropped fitting. counts therefore differ models (e.g. Fully adjusted typically fewer participants Unadjusted). default, assoc_coxph() uses test = "wald" term-level Wald p-values. Set test = "lrt" return exposure-level likelihood-ratio p-value single-term deletion. cluster_col supplied cluster-robust Cox variance, test = "wald" supported.
code: # Crude + age-sex adjusted (automatic); p21022 and p31 auto-detected res <- assoc_coxph(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = c("p20116_i0", "bmi_cat") ) # Add a Fully adjusted model res <- assoc_coxph(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p20116_i0",   covariates   = c("bmi_cat", "tdi_cat", "p1558_i0",                    paste0("p22009_a", 1:10)) )

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: assoc_logistic() binary outcomes without time dimension (e.g. case-control cross-sectional designs). sparse data small samples, use profile likelihood confidence intervals: Output identical structure assoc_coxph() OR_label place HR / HR_label, n_cases instead n_events / person_years.
code: res <- assoc_logistic(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   exposure_col = c("p20116_i0", "bmi_cat"),   covariates   = c("tdi_cat", "p1558_i0", paste0("p22009_a", 1:10)) ) res <- assoc_logistic(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   exposure_col = "grs_bmi",   ci_method    = "profile"   # slower but more accurate for sparse data )

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: assoc_linear() continuous outcomes (e.g. biomarker levels, BMI). standard error beta included support downstream meta-analysis. Common mistake: passing binary (0/1) logical column outcome_col permitted (linear probability model) triggers warning. Use assoc_logistic() binary outcomes — linear regression 0/1 outcome produces unbounded predictions rarely appropriate epidemiological analyses.
code: # Continuous outcome (BMI); smoking and GRS as exposures res <- assoc_linear(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "p21001_i0",   exposure_col = c("p20116_i0", "grs_bmi"),   covariates   = c("tdi_cat", "p1558_i0", paste0("p22009_a", 1:10)) )

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: assoc_coxph_zph() re-fits Cox models tests PH assumption via Schoenfeld residuals (cox.zph()). Use alongside assoc_coxph() validate model assumptions. Output columns include chisq, df, p_value, ph_satisfied (logical), global test statistics (global_chisq, global_df, global_p). PH assumption violated, consider adding strata() assoc_coxph() modelling time-varying effects.
code: zph <- assoc_coxph_zph(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = c("p20116_i0", "bmi_cat"),   covariates   = c("tdi_cat", "p1558_i0") )  # Identify any violations zph[ph_satisfied == FALSE]

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: assoc_subgroup() stratifies dataset grouping variable fits specified model within subgroup. likelihood ratio test (LRT) exposure x subgroup interaction computed full dataset appended p_interaction. Output columns include subgroup, subgroup_level, p_interaction addition standard effect estimate columns. Note: variable automatically excluded subgroup models. include covariates — collinearity warning issued . Subgroup analysis interpretable small number levels (e.g. sex, smoking status); continuous variables technically permitted per-unique-value subgrouping rarely meaningful practice — use pre-categorised version (e.g. via derive_cut()) instead.
code: # Subgroup by sex; p31 is automatically excluded from within-stratum models res <- assoc_subgroup(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p20116_i0",   by           = "p31",   method       = "coxph",   covariates   = c("p21022", "bmi_cat", "tdi_cat") )

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: assoc_trend() fits categorical trend models simultaneously ordered-factor exposure, returning per-category estimates alongside p-value linear trend. Supply custom scores reflecting approximate median BMI per category: output contains reference row (HR = 1.00 (ref)) followed non-reference rows, HR_per_score, HR_per_score_label, p_trend appended shared columns. trend columns carry value across every row within exposure × model combination — including reference row — full result table remains self-contained easy filter export.
code: # assoc_trend() requires an ordered factor; make bmi_cat ordered in-place dt[, bmi_cat := factor(bmi_cat, levels = levels(bmi_cat), ordered = TRUE)] res <- assoc_trend(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "bmi_cat",   method       = "coxph",   covariates   = c("p21022", "p31", "tdi_cat", "p20116_i0") ) res <- assoc_trend(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "bmi_cat",   method       = "coxph",   covariates   = c("p21022", "p31", "tdi_cat", "p20116_i0"),   scores       = c(17, 22, 27, 35)   # approximate median BMI per category )

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: assoc_trend() summarises ordered categorical exposure single linear-trend estimate, assoc_rcs() models full — possibly non-linear — shape continuous exposure using restricted cubic splines. returns prediction curve (one row per grid point) together overall-association p-value p-value non-linearity, capturing U-shaped, J-shaped, threshold, plateau relationships single linear term miss. supports three methods ("coxph", "logistic", "linear") base / covariates adjustment logic rest assoc_* family. exposure must continuous; reference value (ref, default median) effect equals 1 (HR / ) 0 (mean difference). result holds fitted curve (x, estimate, conf_low, conf_high), p_overall p_nonlinear values (repeated within model), plus hidden measure / knots / ref attributes. base = TRUE (default), one curve returned per adjustment model. Pass result straight plot_rcs() draw dose-response curve — see vignette("plot"). Requires rms package (Suggests dependency): assoc_rcs() fits spline rms::cph() / rms::lrm() / rms::ols(), non-linearity test follows canonical Harrell RCS workflow. Install install.packages("rms").
code: res <- assoc_rcs(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p21001_i0",              # BMI (continuous)   method       = "coxph",   covariates   = c("p21022", "p31", "tdi_cat", "p20116_i0"),   knots        = 4,                        # Harrell quantile knots (3-5 typical)   ref          = 25                        # centre the curve at BMI 25 (HR = 1) )

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: assoc_competing() fits Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model via survival::finegray() + inverse-probability--censoring-weighted Cox regression. Use competing event (e.g. death) can preclude outcome interest. Two input modes supported: Mode — single column encodes event types: Mode B — separate 0/1 columns primary competing events: Output uses SHR (subdistribution hazard ratio) SHR_label place HR, adds n_compete (number competing events analysis set).
code: # Construct a combined event column: 0 = censored, 1 = DM, 2 = HTN (competing) dt_cr <- dt[htn_timing != 1L]   # also exclude prevalent HTN dt_cr[, event_type := data.table::fcase(   dm_timing  == 2L, 1L,   htn_timing == 2L, 2L,   default          = 0L )]  res <- assoc_competing(   data         = dt_cr,   outcome_col  = "event_type",       # 0 = censored, 1 = DM, 2 = HTN   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p20116_i0",   event_val    = 1L,   compete_val  = 2L,   covariates   = c("bmi_cat", "tdi_cat") ) res <- assoc_competing(   data         = dt_cr,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",        # primary event   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = c("p20116_i0", "bmi_cat"),   compete_col  = "htn_status",       # competing event   covariates   = c("tdi_cat", "p1558_i0") )

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: functions return data.table feeds directly plot_forest():
code: res <- assoc_coxph(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p20116_i0",   covariates   = c("bmi_cat", "tdi_cat", "p1558_i0") )  # Pass directly to plot_forest() — est/CI/columns auto-derived plot_forest(res)  # Filter to a single model res[model == "Fully adjusted"]  # Export data.table::fwrite(res, "assoc_results.csv")

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: assoc_lag() re-runs Cox models one lag periods assess whether associations driven early events (reverse causation detection bias). lag, participants whose follow-time less lag_years excluded; follow-kept original scale. Setting lag_years = 0 (including 0 vector) runs model full unfiltered cohort, providing reference row lagged results can compared. Output adds two columns standard assoc_coxph() result:
code: res <- assoc_lag(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p20116_i0",   lag_years    = c(0, 1, 2),   # 0 = full cohort reference   covariates   = c("bmi_cat", "tdi_cat", "p1558_i0") )

title: Association Analysis for UKB Outcomes
text: Observational associations can always questioned grounds unmeasured confounding. assoc_evalue() quantifies concern E-value (VanderWeele & Ding, 2017): minimum strength association — risk-ratio scale — unmeasured confounder need exposure outcome, beyond measured covariates, fully explain away observed effect. larger E-value means robust finding; benchmark strongly measured confounders (plausible unmeasured one) associate outcome. reports two numbers per estimate: E-value point estimate, E-value confidence limit closest null (1 interval already spans null). Pass Cox logistic result straight — HR/CI columns read automatically, two columns (evalue_point, evalue_ci) appended: rare-outcome assumption matters: E-value defined risk-ratio scale, hazard odds ratio used directly outcome rare; common outcome first converted RR. result mode prevalence inferred n_events/n (n_cases/n) outcome treated rare 15%; use rare = TRUE/FALSE override. can also evaluate single hand-entered estimate — e.g. one reported another paper — argument names matching plot_forest(): Linear (beta) competing-risks (SHR) results supported; E-value needs ratio effect measure.
code: res <- assoc_coxph(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p20116_i0"            # smoking status )  assoc_evalue(res) assoc_evalue(est = 2.0, lower = 1.5, upper = 2.7, measure = "HR", rare = TRUE)

text: audit_flowchart() turns snapshots layer data.frame shape flowchart renderer expects — five columns, id/parent/n/label/type — without committing particular renderer. produces data; render anything . id several rows merge (row contributes one upstream node); parent several rows branch. label stays plain text count stays n, renderer composes "(n = 1,272)" , whatever style figure calls . default snapshot’s parent previous label recording order – simple linear attrition chain – row count decrease parent child inserted sibling type = "exclusion" row (even decrease zero), matching convention exclusion box sits alongside continuing step rather replacing . genuine branch (e.g. randomisation two arms), declare second later branches’ true parent parent, since default assumption (“parent = previous label”) wrong anything first branch: branch never gets automatic exclusion row (split exclusion), children’s counts checked parent’s warning issued sum – likewise single child’s count somehow larger parent’s, since valid exclusion either.

Two working modes supported: Local → RAP: Run R locally, authenticate DNAnexus API token, interact RAP remotely. RAP → RAP: Run R inside RAP cloud environment (e.g., RStudio DNAnexus), authentication handled automatically platform.

text: disease case definitions derived (see vignette("derive")), three additional functions prepare data time--event analysis: Prerequisite: {name}_status {name}_date must already present — produced vignette("derive"). examples assume full disease derivation pipeline run ops_toy() dataset, baseline date column p53_i0 age recruitment p21022.

what: Step 1: Classify Timing — Prevalent vs. Incident
title: Survival Analysis Setup for UKB Outcomes
text: derive_timing() compares disease date UKB baseline assessment date assigns participant one four categories: Supply explicit column names defaults apply: Call per variable needed — example, combined case per individual source (HES, self-report, etc.).
code: library(ukbflow)  # Build on the derive pipeline from vignette("derive") df <- ops_toy(n = 500) df <- derive_missing(df) df <- derive_covariate(df, as_factor = c("p31", "p20116_i0")) df <- derive_selfreport(df, name = "dm", regex = "type 2 diabetes") df <- derive_icd10(df, name = "dm", icd10 = "E11", source = c("hes", "death")) df <- derive_case(df, name = "dm") # Uses {name}_status and {name}_date by default df <- derive_timing(df, name = "dm", baseline_col = "p53_i0") df <- derive_timing(df,   name         = "dm",   status_col   = "dm_status",   date_col     = "dm_date",   baseline_col = "p53_i0" )

text: derive_age() computes age time event cases, returns NA non-cases cases without date. age_at_event=age_at_recruitment+event_date−baseline_date365.25\text{age\_at\_event} = \text{age\_at\_recruitment} + \frac{\text{event\_date} - \text{baseline\_date}}{365.25} divisor 365.25 accounts leap years, ensuring sub-monthly precision age calculation across full UKB follow-window. Supply explicit column mappings names follow default {name}_date / {name}_status pattern:
code: # Auto-detects {name}_date and {name}_status; produces age_at_{name} column. df <- derive_age(df,   name         = "dm",   baseline_col = "p53_i0",   age_col      = "p21022" ) df <- derive_age(df,   name         = "dm",   baseline_col = "p53_i0",   age_col      = "p21022",   date_cols    = c(dm = "dm_date"),   status_cols  = c(dm = "dm_status") )

title: Deriving Disease Phenotypes from UKB Data
text: derive_selfreport() searches UKB self-reported non-cancer illness (field 20002) cancer (field 20001) columns disease label matching regex, returns binary status earliest report date. Column detection automatic field IDs. adds two columns per call:
code: # Non-cancer: type 2 diabetes (field 20002) df <- derive_selfreport(df,   name  = "dm",   regex = "type 2 diabetes" ) # Cancer: lung cancer (field 20001) df <- derive_selfreport(df,   name  = "lung_cancer",   regex = "lung cancer",   field = "cancer" )

title: Deriving Disease Phenotypes from UKB Data
text: derive_hes() scans UKB Hospital Episode Statistics ICD-10 codes (field 41270, stored JSON array per participant) matches earliest corresponding date field 41280. default (position = "") derive_hes() uses field 41270, contains ICD-10 codes recorded diagnosis position, matching code counts case. Pass position = "main" restrict primary diagnoses (fields 41202 / 41262). Secondary-selection offered UKB provides aligned per-code date field secondary diagnoses (field 41204). match argument controls codes compared:
code: # Prefix match: codes starting with "I10" (hypertension) df <- derive_hes(df, name = "htn", icd10 = "I10")  # Exact match df <- derive_hes(df, name = "dm_hes", icd10 = "E11", match = "exact")  # Regex: E10 and E11 simultaneously df <- derive_hes(df, name = "dm_broad", icd10 = "^E1[01]", match = "regex")

title: Deriving Disease Phenotypes from UKB Data
text: minority HES records — mostly older Scottish records predate UK-wide transition ICD-10 — coded ICD-9. derive_hes_icd9() ICD-9 counterpart derive_hes(), identical field structure shifted parallel ICD-9 fields: 41271 / 41281 -position diagnoses, 41203 / 41263 main-diagnosis-. match position arguments, semantics. Output columns named dem9_hes_icd9 / dem9_hes_icd9_date — separate suffix derive_hes()’s _hes / _hes_date — ICD-10 ICD-9 call phenotype name can run without one overwriting ’s columns.
code: df <- derive_hes_icd9(df, name = "dem9", icd9 = c("331.0", "290.4"))

title: Deriving Disease Phenotypes from UKB Data
text: HES also records operations procedures OPCS-4, parallel field pair diagnosis fields: 41272 / 41282 -position codes, 41200 / 41260 main procedure . derive_opcs() OPCS-4 counterpart derive_hes(), match position arguments semantics. OPCS-4 codes stored dotted format, like ICD-10 (e.g. K40, K23.4), transcribe paper written — match = "prefix" 3-character category K40 matches children (K40.1, K40.2, …). Output columns named cabg_opcs / cabg_opcs_date, separate suffix , diagnosis procedure call name coexist.
code: # Coronary revascularisation procedures (the K40 category matches K40.1, etc.) df <- derive_opcs(df, name = "cabg", opcs = c("K40", "K41", "K44", "K45"))

title: Deriving Disease Phenotypes from UKB Data
text: Primary-care (GP) clinical events live gp_clinical record table (UKB Record Table 1060), participant fields — one row per coded event, ~118M rows across ~45% cohort. carries two coding systems two columns: Read v2 read_2 (England Vision, Scotland, Wales) CTV3 / Read v3 read_3 (England TPP). separate coding systems — like ICD-10 vs ICD-9 HES — handled two functions code lists: derive_gp_read2() derive_gp_ctv3(). gp_clinical separate long table, pass gp (loaded extract_gp(), reused across calls). Read v2 codes 5-character, dot-padded case-sensitive; CTV3 codes opaque identifiers, default match = "exact" (prefix meaningful Read v2’s positional hierarchy CTV3). ops_toy(scenario = "gp") returns synthetic table columns, GP path can exercised offline. Use n seed cohort call eid values line : RAP calls take real table extract_gp(): Output columns t2d_gp_read2 / t2d_gp_ctv3 (plus _date). UKB placeholder event dates (Coding 819: 1901-01-01, 1902-02-02, …) still count status never supply date.
code: # gp is the gp_clinical long table: eid, data_provider, read_2, read_3, event_dt # Same n and seed as the ops_toy(n = 500) cohort above, so the eids line up gp <- ops_toy(scenario = "gp", n = 500)  df <- derive_gp_read2(df, name = "t2d", read2 = c("C1041", "C10F6"), gp = gp) df <- derive_gp_ctv3 (df, name = "t2d", ctv3  = "XaELQ",             gp = gp) gp <- extract_gp()   # load gp_clinical once, reuse across calls df <- derive_gp_read2(df, name = "t2d", read2 = c("C10F.", "C10F0"), gp = gp) df <- derive_gp_ctv3 (df, name = "t2d", ctv3  = "XaELP",             gp = gp)

title: Deriving Disease Phenotypes from UKB Data
text: UKB First Occurrence fields (p131xxx) record earliest date condition observed across linked sources — self-report, HES inpatient, GP records, death registry — pre-integrated UKB. Look disease UKB Field Finder.
code: # ops_toy includes p131742 as a representative First Occurrence column df <- derive_first_occurrence(df, name = "htn", field = 131742L, col = "p131742")

text: minority cancer registrations (older records) coded ICD-9 (field 40013) instead ICD-10 (40006). derive_cancer_registry_icd9() matches 40013 reuses histology (40011), behaviour (40012), diagnosis-date (40005) fields ICD-10 arm — given registration instance carries code either 40006 40013, never , date/histology/behaviour live shared fields instance number. 40013 fewer instances 40006 (smaller, legacy minority), instances matched registration number rather array position, size difference causes misalignment. title: Deriving Disease Phenotypes from UKB Data
text: phenotypes best ascertained raw codes UK Biobank’s algorithmically-defined outcomes (ADOs, Category 42): adjudicated Date fields — e.g. 42018 (-cause dementia), 42006 (stroke), 42016 (COPD) — UKB already reconciled across self-report, HES, death records. derive_algorithm() reads one Date field produces {name}_alg status flag {name}_alg_date. ops_toy() ships p42018 (-cause dementia), including rows carrying 1900-01-01 sentinel — self-report-case unknown onset year. sentinel deliberately filtered NA count case, every positive case carries usable date: ADO self-contained: {name}_alg / {name}_alg_date already final case definition, adjudication reconciles sources internally. Feed two columns straight assoc_* via outcome_col / time_col. route ADO derive_case() pass derive_icd10() (ICD-10 code source), pair separate derive_selfreport() phenotype — double-count self-report admit date algorithm deliberately excluded.

Single-source case definitions also possible. Five workflows available: extract_batch() recommended approach serious analysis. extract_pheno() provided quick interactive inspection inside RAP environment . distinction decides function need fields versus record-table entities: extract_batch(), extract_pheno() extract_nmr() pull participant-level fields (p31, p53_i0, p23400_i0, …), matched field ID. extract_gp() extract_olink() export whole record-table entity — gp_clinical, olink_instance_0 — whose columns participant fields , field-ID matching . title: Extracting Phenotype Data
text: Primary-care data set participant fields — lives separate record-table entities (gp_clinical, gp_scripts, gp_registrations), one row per clinical event. extract_gp() exports whole entity via table-exporter job returns raw long table (date parsing, code matching, filtering — derive_gp_read2() / derive_gp_ctv3()’s job). runs inside RAP environment; export runs worker instance (default mem1_ssd1_v2_x16), gp_clinical (~118M rows, ~3 GB) typically takes 10-15 minutes.

text: Olink NPX data lives olink_instance_{0,2,3} entities — baseline two imaging visits. wide record table: one column per protein (~2900, named assay, e.g. a1bg) plus eid. extract_olink() discovers entity’s columns rather hardcoding protein names, exports , returns raw wide table eid moved front. Prerequisite: field 30900 (“Number proteins measured”) must project basket unlock Olink entities. per-sample QC fields (p30901 plate, p30902 well) ordinary participant fields — pull extract_batch() need .
code: # Whole baseline panel (~2900 proteins) olink <- extract_olink()  # One of the imaging visits olink_i2 <- extract_olink(instance = 2)  # A named subset, skipping column discovery inflam <- extract_olink(columns = c("eid", "crp", "il6"))

title: Genetic Risk Score (GRS) Analysis on UKB RAP
text: grs_* functions provide end--end pipeline computing validating polygenic / genetic risk scores within UK Biobank Research Analysis Platform (RAP). individual-level genotype data downloaded locally, computationally intensive steps executed cloud jobs via DNAnexus Swiss Army Knife app. Typical pipeline: Prerequisite: must authenticated UKB RAP project selected. See vignette("auth").
code: grs_check()  ->  grs_bgen2pgen()  ->  grs_score()  ->  grs_standardize()  ->  grs_validate()

what: Step 1: Validate the Weights File – grs_check()
title: Genetic Risk Score (GRS) Analysis on UKB RAP
text: uploading RAP, validate SNP weights file. function reads file, checks required columns, flags problems, writes plink2-compatible space-delimited output. Required columns: validated weights also returned invisibly inspection.
code: library(ukbflow)  # Local: weights file on your machine w <- grs_check("weights.csv", dest = "weights_clean.txt") #> Read 'weights.csv': 312 rows, 5 columns. #> ✔ No NA values. #> ✔ No duplicate SNPs. #> ✔ All SNP IDs match rs[0-9]+ format. #> ✔ All effect alleles are A/T/C/G. #> Beta summary: #>   Range     : -0.412 to 0.589 #>   Mean |beta|: 0.183 #>   Positive  : 187 (59.9%) #>   Negative  : 125 (40.1%) #>   Zero      : 0 #> ✔ Weights file passed checks: 312 SNPs ready for UKB RAP. #> ✔ Saved: 'weights_clean.txt' # On RAP (RStudio) -- use /mnt/project/ paths directly w <- grs_check(   file = "/mnt/project/weights/weights.csv",   dest = "/mnt/project/weights/weights_clean.txt" )

what: Step 2: Convert BGEN to PGEN – grs_bgen2pgen()
title: Genetic Risk Score (GRS) Analysis on UKB RAP
text: UKB imputed genotype data stored BGEN format RAP. grs_bgen2pgen() submits one Swiss Army Knife job per chromosome convert BGEN files plink2-native PGEN format MAF filter applied via plink2. staged workflow separates one-time genotype conversion repeated GRS scoring, converted PGEN files can reused across multiple score files. trade-additional RAP project storage: PGEN outputs kept reused, removed according project’s storage cost policy longer needed. function called local machine RAP RStudio – heavy lifting runs entirely cloud. Instance types: Key arguments: Storage warning: chromosomes 1–16 may exceed 200 GB SSD "standard" instances. Use instance = "large" .

title: Installation Guide
text: ukbflow R package UK Biobank data analysis visualization, designed work natively UK Biobank Research Analysis Platform (RAP). supports two working modes: Local → RAP: Run R locally, authenticate DNAnexus, submit jobs, download summary results. RAP → RAP: Run R directly inside RAP cloud environment, authentication handled automatically. UK Biobank Data Policy (2024+): Individual-level phenotype genotype data must remain within RAP environment downloaded locally. summary-level outputs (aggregated statistics, plots, reports) may exported.

title: One Phenotype, Many Definitions: A Reproducibility and Comparability Case Study
text: UK Biobank studies routinely report outcome name — “stroke”, “type 2 diabetes” — describe ascertained sentence two, supplementary table. Yet several studies define named phenotype, operational definitions frequently disagree: codes, data sources, matching rule, whether fatal events count, whether self-report primary-care records included. choices often implicit, scattered across supplements, simply stated. creates reproducibility comparability problem two related forms: Documented--divergent — definitions written (usually supplementary tables), genuinely differ. definition can reproduced within study, interchangeable others; cross-study comparability problem, sloppy reporting. -documented — definition recovered paper : data source named field/codes published, even within-study reproduction limited. distinction matters. Documented divergence necessarily prevent within-study reproduction; instead, prevents readers treating identically named outcomes harmonised across studies. -documentation stronger reproducibility failure, original definition reconstructed. vignette works , using bundled recipe_* library evidence base. Everything computed offline shipped recipe files — UK Biobank data accessed, published result recomputed. case study reproduce published findings. demonstrates phenotype name can refer non-interchangeable definitions. recipe records phenotype operationally defined — sources, codes, matching rules, caveats. recipe may encode fully reported definition, document incomplete one, include explicitly labelled curator inference publication -specified. Recipes read-versioned; see vignette("recipe") schema vignette("derive") applying one data derive_recipe().

Within coded sources represented recipe, identify fatal stroke recorded death registry never inpatient record. stroke_vazquez uses none codes: takes UK Biobank algorithmically-defined stroke outcome (field 42006), case set whatever UKB Outcomes Adjudication Group’s algorithm returns. Whether I62 counts stroke differs. stroke_lu, stroke_qin, stroke_yun include I62; stroke, stroke_mu, stroke_nyberg . matching rule differs. stroke_mu enumerates parent child codes matches exactly; others match ICD-10 prefix. code: summarise_def <- function(id) {   src <- suppressMessages(recipe_sources(id))    icd10 <- unlist(strsplit(stats::na.omit(src$icd10), ","))   icd9  <- unlist(strsplit(stats::na.omit(src$icd9),  ","))    data.table(     id         = id,     sources    = paste(sort(unique(src$source)), collapse = " + "),     icd10_match = paste(unique(stats::na.omit(src$match)), collapse = "/"),     includes_I62 = any(grepl("^I62", icd10)),     n_icd10_codes = length(unique(icd10)),     icd9 = if (length(icd9)) paste(unique(icd9), collapse = ",") else "—"   ) }  comparison <- rbindlist(lapply(stroke_ids, summarise_def)) comparison[] #>                id                                     sources icd10_match #>            <char>                                      <char>      <char> #> 1:         stroke                                 death + hes      prefix #> 2:      stroke_lu death + first_occurrence + hes + selfreport      prefix #> 3:      stroke_mu                                 death + hes       exact #> 4:  stroke_nyberg                      death + hes + hes_icd9      prefix #> 5:     stroke_qin                                 death + hes      prefix #> 6: stroke_vazquez                                   algorithm             #> 7:     stroke_yun                              hes + hes_icd9      prefix #>    includes_I62 n_icd10_codes                    icd9 #>          <lgcl>         <int>                  <char> #> 1:        FALSE             4                       — #> 2:         TRUE            32                       — #> 3:        FALSE            35                       — #> 4:        FALSE             4     430,431,433,434,436 #> 5:         TRUE             5                       — #> 6:        FALSE             0                       — #> 7:         TRUE             5 430,431,432,433,434,436

title: Publication-Ready Visualisation
text: plot_forest() takes data frame whose first column row label, plus additional display columns. CI graphic formatted (95% CI) text column inserted automatically.
code: library(ukbflow)  df <- data.frame(   item      = c("Exposure vs. control", "Unadjusted", "Fully adjusted"),   `Cases/N` = c("", "89 / 4 521", "89 / 4 521"),   p_value   = c(NA_real_, 0.001, 0.006),   check.names = FALSE )  p <- plot_forest(   data      = df,   est       = c(NA,   1.52, 1.43),   lower     = c(NA,   1.18, 1.11),   upper     = c(NA,   1.96, 1.85),   ci_column = 3L,   indent    = c(0L,   1L,   1L),   p_cols    = "p_value",   xlim      = c(0.5,  3.0) ) plot(p)

Pass "" gap column position. align controls per-column text alignment across ncol(data) + 2 columns: -1 = left, 0 = centre, 1 = right. NULL (default) left-aligns column 1 centres rest. Background borders Layout saving four formats (PNG, PDF, JPG, TIFF) written 300 dpi white background. function returns plot object invisibly; display plot(p) grid::grid.draw(p).
code: # uses df, est, lower, upper from the minimal example above p <- plot_forest(   data      = df,   est       = est, lower = lower, upper = upper,   ci_column = 3L,   ci_col    = c("grey50", "steelblue", "steelblue"),  # per-row colours   ci_sizes  = 0.5,       # point size   ci_Theight = 0.15,     # cap height   ref_line  = 1,         # reference line (use 0 for beta coefficients)   xlim      = c(0.2, 5), ticks_at = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3) ) # indent = 0 → bold parent row; indent >= 1 → indented sub-row (plain) p <- plot_forest(   data       = df,   est        = est, lower = lower, upper = upper,   ci_column  = 3L,   indent     = c(0L, 1L, 1L),        # parent + 2 sub-rows   bold_label = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)  # explicit control (overrides indent default) ) # p_cols: column names in data that contain raw numeric p-values. # Values < 10^(-p_digits) are displayed as e.g. "<0.001". # bold_p = TRUE bolds all p < p_threshold (default 0.05). p <- plot_forest(   data        = df,   est         = est, lower = lower, upper = upper,   ci_column   = 3L,   p_cols      = "p_value",   p_digits    = 3L,   bold_p      = TRUE,   p_threshold = 0.05 ) # data has 3 columns → final table has 5 columns (original 3 + gap_ci + OR label) # Layout with ci_column = 3L: item | Cases/N | gap_ci | OR (95% CI) | p_value p <- plot_forest(   data      = df,   est       = est, lower = lower, upper = upper,   ci_column = 3L,   header    = c("Comparison", "Cases / N", "", "HR (95% CI)", "P-value")   #             col 1          col 2        gap  OR label       col 5 ) p <- plot_forest(   data      = df,   est       = est, lower = lower, upper = upper,   ci_column = 3L,   align     = c(-1L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 1L)   # label left | Cases/N centre | gap | OR centre | p right ) p <- plot_forest(   data       = df,   est        = est, lower = lower, upper = upper,   ci_column  = 3L,   background = "zebra",       # "zebra" | "bold_label" | "none"   bg_col     = "#F0F0F0",     # shading colour   border     = "three_line",  # "three_line" | "none"   border_width = 3            # scalar or length-3 vector (top / mid / bottom) ) # uses df, est, lower, upper from the minimal example above p <- plot_forest(   data        = df,   est         = est, lower = lower, upper = upper,   ci_column   = 3L,   row_height  = NULL,   # auto (8 / 12 / 10 / 15 mm); or scalar/vector   col_width   = NULL,   # auto (rounds up to nearest 5 mm)   save        = TRUE,   dest        = "forest_main",   # extension ignored; all 4 formats saved   save_width  = 20,              # cm   save_height = NULL             # auto: nrow(data) * 0.9 + 3 cm )

title: Publication-Ready Visualisation
text: Variable types statistics SMD column SMD column summarises covariate balance groups: - Continuous variables: Cohen’s d (pooled-SD formula) - Categorical variables: RMSD group proportions Excluding rows Use exclude_labels remove specific level rows rendered table (e.g. redundant reference category “Unknown” level): Themes theme = "default" (default) renders clean three-line table cell shading — safe choice journal submission. theme = "lancet" adds alternating pink row shading shaded header. keep bold variable labels, three-line borders, 15 px font. Export formats save = TRUE, four files written simultaneously: PDF PNG rendering requires pagedown webshot2 respectively. Install install.packages(c("pagedown", "webshot2")).
code: dt <- as.data.frame(ops_toy(scenario = "association"))  plot_tableone(   data      = dt,   vars      = c("p21022", "p21001_i0", "p31", "p20116_i0"),   strata    = "dm_status",   type      = list(p21022 = "continuous2"),   # show median + IQR   statistic = list(     all_continuous()  ~ "{mean} ({sd})",     all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"   ),   digits    = list(p21022 ~ 1, p21001_i0 ~ 1),   missing   = "ifany",   # show missing counts when present   save      = FALSE ) plot_tableone(   data    = dt,   vars    = c("p21022", "p21001_i0", "p31"),   strata  = "dm_status",   add_smd = TRUE,   save    = FALSE ) plot_tableone(   data           = dt,   vars           = c("p31", "p20116_i0"),   strata         = "dm_status",   exclude_labels = "Never",   # e.g. remove reference category from display   save           = FALSE ) plot_tableone(   data   = trial,   vars   = c("age", "marker", "grade"),   strata = "trt",   theme  = "lancet",   # or "default" (no shading)   save   = FALSE )

title: Publication-Ready Visualisation
text: plot_survival() draws publication-ready Kaplan-Meier curve. takes analysis data plus follow--time column event-status column (optionally grouping column); survfit model fitted internally, Surv() object needed. interface mirrors assoc_coxph(), inputs exactly derive_followup() derive_case() produce. non-parametric, unadjusted estimate computed straight three columns — use Cox model covariates. adjusted hazard ratios, use plot_forest() assoc_coxph() result instead. plot_survival() builds ggsurvfit (Suggests dependency); install install.packages(c("ggsurvfit", "ggplot2")).

title: Publication-Ready Visualisation
text: default figure includes confidence-interval ribbon, numbers--risk table, log-rank p-value. strata, single overall curve drawn p-value omitted.
code: library(survival)  lung2 <- lung lung2$sex <- factor(lung2$sex, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female"))  plot_survival(   data       = lung2,   time_col   = "time",   status_col = "status",   # 1/2 coding -> auto-normalised to 0/1   strata     = "sex",   xlab       = "Time (days)" )

title: Publication-Ready Visualisation
text: type switches descending survival curve ascending cumulative views:
code: # Cumulative incidence (1 - S) plot_survival(lung2, "time", "status", strata = "sex", type = "risk")  # Cumulative hazard plot_survival(lung2, "time", "status", strata = "sex", type = "cumhaz")

title: Publication-Ready Visualisation
text: Toggle optional layers add_* switches, adjust axis, labels, palette, legend: theme preset ("default") controls overall look — fonts, legend, colour palette, risk-table styling — one coherent design. default palette used colour every group; groups colours falls back ggsurvfit’s palette.
code: plot_survival(   lung2, "time", "status", strata = "sex",   add_median  = TRUE,          # median-survival reference line   add_censor  = TRUE,          # censoring marks   ticks_at    = seq(0, 1000, 250),   palette     = c("#3C5488", "#F39B7F"),   legend_labs = c("Male", "Female"),   title       = "Overall survival by sex" )

title: Publication-Ready Visualisation
code: # Writes <dest>.png / .pdf / .jpg / .tiff at 300 dpi plot_survival(lung2, "time", "status", strata = "sex",               save = TRUE, dest = "km_lung_by_sex")

title: Publication-Ready Visualisation
text: plot_rcs() draws dose-response curve produced assoc_rcs(): fitted effect (hazard ratio, odds ratio, mean difference) across range continuous exposure, confidence band, relative analysis reference value. reads effect measure, reference, exposure name result’s attributes, plot_rcs(res) just works. plot_rcs() builds ggplot2 (Suggests dependency); install install.packages("ggplot2"). Unlike plot functions returns ggplot object visibly, bare plot_rcs(res) call draws curve.

title: Publication-Ready Visualisation
text: null-effect line (HR / = 1, 0 mean difference) drawn automatically, y-axis log-scaled ratio measures, overall non-linearity p-values annotated corner P-overall / P-nonlinear. panel uses clean framed style light horizontal grid.
code: res <- assoc_rcs(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p21001_i0",          # BMI (continuous)   method       = "coxph",   base         = FALSE,                # a single, fully-adjusted curve   covariates   = "tdi_cat" )  plot_rcs(res)

title: Publication-Ready Visualisation
text: vline hline add user-supplied reference lines clinically meaningful exposure effect values — dashed grey, spirit threshold lines GWAS plot:
code: plot_rcs(   res,   vline = c(18.5, 25, 30),   # clinical BMI cut-points (x-axis)   hline = 1.5,               # an effect threshold (y-axis)   p_pos = "topleft",         # move the p-value annotation   title = "BMI and incident diabetes" )

title: Publication-Ready Visualisation
text: assoc_rcs() result holds one adjustment model (default base = TRUE), curves overlaid coloured model, legend bottom; p-value annotation reports -adjusted model:
code: res_multi <- assoc_rcs(   dt, "dm_status", "dm_followup_years", "p21001_i0",   # BMI   method = "coxph", covariates = "tdi_cat" )  plot_rcs(res_multi, vline = c(18.5, 25, 30))

title: Recipe Catalog: The Phenotype Definition Library
text: ukbflow ships versioned library reproducible UK Biobank phenotype definitions (“recipes”). recipe records phenotype ascertained published study (standard definition): data sources, codes, reconciliation logic, caveats matter reproducing . page live catalog library — table generated build time directly installed recipes, always reflects current contents. use recipes (recipe_list(), recipe_get(), recipe_sources()) write one (recipe_new()), see vignette("recipe"); data sources code systems recipes draw , see vignette("phenotype-scope").

title: Recipe Catalog: The Phenotype Definition Library
text: 67 phenotype recipes currently library. Coverage Full every arm published definition executable ukbflow, Partial one reported components documented recipe notes executable. See vignette("phenotype-scope") current support boundaries.
code: library(ukbflow)  # Prettify the fixed source-slot names for display. slot_labels <- c(   selfreport            = "Self-report",   hes                   = "HES",   hes_icd9              = "HES (ICD-9)",   opcs                  = "HES (OPCS-4)",   gp_read2              = "GP (Read v2)",   gp_ctv3               = "GP (CTV3)",   death                 = "Death",   first_occurrence      = "First Occurrence",   cancer_registry       = "Cancer registry",   cancer_registry_icd9  = "Cancer registry (ICD-9)",   algorithm             = "Algorithm" )  catalog <- do.call(rbind, lapply(recipe_list()$id, function(id) {   r <- recipe_get(id)    # Source slots actually used by this recipe (non-empty rule lists).   used  <- names(r$sources)[vapply(r$sources, length, integer(1)) > 0L]   used  <- slot_labels[used]    # Provenance: the first note, trimmed to author + year + journal.   notes <- unlist(r$notes)   prov  <- sub("^Provenance: ", "", notes[1])   prov  <- sub(" DOI.*$", "", prov)      # drop DOI / PMID / trailing detail   prov  <- sub("[,.] *$", "", prov)    # Coverage: full unless a note records an arm ukbflow cannot execute   # (recorded verbatim but "not applied" / "not currently supported", etc.).   gap <- any(grepl(     "COVERAGE|not applied|not executed|not executable|not currently supported",     notes, ignore.case = TRUE   ))    data.frame(     ID         = id,     Phenotype  = r$label,     Sources    = paste(used, collapse = ", "),     Provenance = prov,     Coverage   = if (gap) "Partial — see notes" else "Full",     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) }))  knitr::kable(   catalog,   row.names = FALSE,   caption   = sprintf("%d phenotype recipes currently in the library.",                       nrow(catalog)) )

title: Phenotype Definition Recipes
text: recipe_* functions small, read-library UK Biobank phenotype definitions. recipe records phenotype operationally defined — data sources, codes patterns used, sources combine, caveats matter reproducing . Recipes deliberately limited scope. recipe_* function reads writes cohort — none takes data argument. Three browse inspect library (recipe_list(), recipe_get(), recipe_sources()); three author definition (recipe_rule(), recipe_new(), recipe_write()), file touch definition . library: records definitions versioned YAML — recipe never silently mutates data; applied data single companion function, derive_recipe() (part derive_* family — see vignette("derive")), call explicitly; select recommend “correct” case definition medical reference; ships versioned YAML files (inst/extdata/recipes/*.yaml) definition can cited, compared, contributed . motivation reproducibility. Phenotype definitions UK Biobank studies often described prose, making hard reproduce compare across papers. recipe turns prose structured, inspectable record. Recipes sit alongside audit_* family: audit_* records analysis , recipe_* records phenotype defined. Unlike ukbflow, recipe_* functions run entirely locally need RAP access — examples execute bundled library.

title: Phenotype Definition Recipes
text: recipe_get() reads single recipe id returns normalised ukbflow_recipe object readable print method. recipe_list() tolerant, recipe_get() strict: unknown id structurally invalid recipe raises error reproduced. returned object always shape, makes safe program : eleven source slots present (selfreport, hes, hes_icd9, opcs, gp_read2, gp_ctv3, death, first_occurrence, cancer_registry, cancer_registry_icd9, algorithm), list rules (empty unused); logic carries documented defaults (case = "", date = "earliest") file omits ; notes always character vector.
code: recipe_get("cscc") #>  #> ── Recipe: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) ──────────────────────────── #> id: cscc | version 2 | updated 2026-07-13 #> A UK Biobank operational phenotype definition for cutaneous squamous cell #> carcinoma, based on self-report and cancer-registry records, including C44 #> records with squamous-cell histology and D04 in-situ records. #>  #> Sources #>   • selfreport  field="cancer"  regex="^squamous cell carcinoma$" #>   • cancer_registry #>       - invasive  icd10="^C44"  histology=[13 codes]  behaviour=3 #>       - in_situ  icd10="^D04" #>       - in_situ  icd10="^C44"  histology=[13 codes]  behaviour=2 #>  #> Logic case=any | date=earliest #>  #> Notes #>   1. Cancer-registry cSCC is split into invasive (behaviour 3) and in situ (behaviour 2); in situ additionally includes D04 regardless of histology. #>   2. Behaviour codes: 3 = invasive / malignant, 2 = in situ. #>   3. Self-report cancer dates rely on p20006 and baseline (p53); p40005 is deliberately NOT used to correct them, because p40005 instances may not align with the p40006 cancer-type instance and could borrow another cancer's date. ad <- recipe_get("atopic_dermatitis")  names(ad) #>  [1] "id"          "label"       "short_label" "version"     "created"     #>  [6] "updated"     "description" "sources"     "logic"       "notes" ad$logic #> $case #> [1] "any" #>  #> $date #> [1] "earliest" ad$sources$first_occurrence #> [[1]] #> [[1]]$field #> [1] 131720

title: Phenotype Definition Recipes
text: recipe_sources() flattens recipe tidy data.table, one row per rule, canonical source order. diff-friendly view: well suited comparing different studies operationalised phenotype, supplementary tables manuscript. rule’s fields spread across fixed columns (source, rule, subtype, field, match, position, cause, regex, icd10, icd9, histology, behaviour). histology list-column holding full integer vector codes verbatim — nothing folded counted away, table retains everything needed reproduce definition. Two columns capture source-specific restrictions mirror derive_* arguments. position records HES diagnosis position (derive_hes(position = ): "" -position diagnoses, "main" primary diagnosis ), cause records death-certificate cause used (derive_death_registry(cause = ): "", "primary" underlying cause, "secondary" contributory causes). empty apply default "", recipe sets record deliberate restriction — example, outcome ascertained underlying cause death (cause = "primary").

title: ukbflow
text: Connection — Authenticate RAP via dx-toolkit manage project selection (auth_login, auth_select_project) Data Access — Retrieve phenotype, primary-care, proteomic metabolomic data UKB dataset RAP; monitor asynchronous jobs (extract_batch, extract_gp, extract_olink, extract_nmr, job_wait, job_result) Data Processing — Harmonize multi-source records derive analysis-ready cohort: decode field IDs value codes, build ICD-10 case definitions, compute follow-time (decode_names, decode_values, derive_icd10, derive_followup, derive_case) Association Analysis — Cox, logistic, linear regression automatic three-model adjustment framework; subgroup analysis, categorical spline dose-response, Fine-Gray competing risks, E-value sensitivity unmeasured confounding (assoc_coxph, assoc_logistic, assoc_subgroup, assoc_rcs, assoc_evalue) Genomic Scoring — Distributed plink2 scoring RAP worker nodes: BGEN → PGEN conversion, multi-chromosome GRS computation, standardization (grs_bgen2pgen, grs_score, grs_standardize) Visualization — Publication-ready forest plots, Kaplan-Meier curves, spline dose-response curves, Table 1 outputs common manuscript formats (plot_forest, plot_survival, plot_rcs, plot_tableone) Utilities — Verify environment analysis; search approved project fields, look field IDs offline — common fields plus blood count, blood biochemistry NMR panels full; find field IDs behind First Occurrence algorithmically-defined outcome; browse common covariate presets decoded column names; generate synthetic UKB-like data development; diagnose missing values; track cohort changes across pipeline steps; exclude withdrawn participants (ops_setup, ops_fields, ops_fields_common, ops_fo, ops_alg, ops_covariates, ops_toy, ops_na, ops_snapshot, ops_withdraw) Phenotype Recipes — Browse, inspect, flatten versioned library reproducible phenotype definitions, recording phenotype operationally defined (sources, codes, logic, caveats); apply one cohort single call, author new definition without hand-writing YAML (recipe_list, recipe_get, recipe_sources, derive_recipe, recipe_rule, recipe_new, recipe_write) Analysis Audit — Create lightweight JSON manifests reproducibility: field IDs, dataset snapshots, derived phenotype summaries, versioned phenotype recipes, model result tables, RAP jobs, session metadata; read manifest back compare labelled records two whole audit objects; export cohort attrition table flowchart-rendering package (audit_start, audit_fields, audit_snapshot, audit_pheno, audit_recipe, audit_model, audit_job, audit_write, audit_read, audit_diff, audit_flowchart)

title: ukbflow

Current public phenotype helpers focus UKB sources listed , including primary-care diagnoses (Read v2 / CTV3); GP prescriptions numeric measurements covered.

title: ukbflow
code: library(ukbflow)  # Open an audit manifest: it records what the analysis did as it runs aud <- audit_start("smoking_lung_cancer")  # Simulate UKB-style data locally (on RAP: replace with extract_batch() + job_wait()) data <- ops_toy(n = 5000, seed = 2026) |>   derive_missing()  # Derive lung cancer outcome (ICD-10 C34) and follow-up time data <- data |>   derive_icd10(name = "lung", icd10 = "C34",                source = c("cancer_registry", "hes")) |>   derive_followup(name         = "lung",                   event_col    = "lung_icd10_date",                   baseline_col = "p53_i0",                   censor_date  = as.Date("2022-10-31"),                   death_col    = "p40000_i0")  # Define exposure: ever vs. never smoker data[, smoking_ever := factor(   ifelse(p20116_i0 == "Never", "Never", "Ever"),   levels = c("Never", "Ever") )]  # Cox regression: smoking → lung cancer (3-model adjustment) res <- assoc_coxph(data,   outcome_col  = "lung_icd10",   time_col     = "lung_followup_years",   exposure_col = "smoking_ever",   covariates   = c("p21022", "p31", "p22189"))  # Forest plot — pass the result straight in; est/CI/columns auto-derived plot_forest(res)  # Record the model and write the manifest: field IDs, cohort snapshots, # phenotype summaries, model results and session metadata, as JSON aud <- audit_model(aud, res) audit_write(aud, "smoking_lung_cancer_audit.json")

title: Fine-Gray competing risks association analysis — assoc_competing

title: Fine-Gray competing risks association analysis — assoc_competing
code: assoc_competing(   data,   outcome_col,   time_col,   exposure_col,   compete_col = NULL,   event_val = 1L,   compete_val = 2L,   covariates = NULL,   base = TRUE,   conf_level = 0.95 )  assoc_fg(   data,   outcome_col,   time_col,   exposure_col,   compete_col = NULL,   event_val = 1L,   compete_val = 2L,   covariates = NULL,   base = TRUE,   conf_level = 0.95 )

title: Fine-Gray competing risks association analysis — assoc_competing
text: data (data.frame data.table) Analysis dataset. outcome_col (character) Primary event column. Mode : multi-value column (integer character codes). Mode B: 0/1 binary column. time_col (character) Follow-time column (numeric, e.g. years). exposure_col (character) One exposure variable names. compete_col (character NULL) Mode B : name 0/1 competing event column. NULL (default), Mode used. event_val Scalar value outcome_col indicating primary event (Mode ). Default: 1L. compete_val Scalar value outcome_col indicating competing event (Mode ). Default: 2L. covariates (character NULL) Covariate names Fully adjusted model. NULL, Unadjusted (Age/sex adjusted base = TRUE) run. base (logical) Whether auto-detect age sex columns standard UKB decoded names include Age sex adjusted model. Default: TRUE. conf_level (numeric) Confidence level SHR intervals. Default: 0.95.

title: Fine-Gray competing risks association analysis — assoc_competing
text: data.table one row per exposure \(\times\) term \(\times\) model combination: exposure Exposure variable name. term Coefficient name returned coxph. model Ordered factor: Unadjusted < Age sex adjusted < Fully adjusted. n Participants model (NA removal). n_events Primary events analysis set. n_compete Competing events analysis set. SHR Subdistribution hazard ratio. CI_lower Lower CI bound. CI_upper Upper CI bound. p_value Robust z-test p-value weighted Cox. SHR_label Formatted string, e.g. "1.23 (1.05-1.44)". returned table also carries hidden attribute recording outcome_col, time_col, covariates, exposure levels, conf_level, competing event encoded (compete_col, event_val, compete_val); audit_model reads automatically.

title: Fine-Gray competing risks association analysis — assoc_competing
text: Two input modes supported depending outcome coded dataset: Mode - single multi-value column compete_col = NULL (default). outcome_col contains event codes one column (e.g. 0/1/2/3). Use event_val compete_val identify event interest competing event; values treated censored. Example: UKB censoring_type 1 = event, 2 = death (competing), 0/3 = censored. Mode B - dual binary columns compete_col name separate 0/1 column competing event. outcome_col 0/1 column primary event. 1 participant, primary event takes priority. Example: outcome_col = "copd_status", compete_col = "death_status". Internally modes converted three-level factor c("censor", "event", "compete") passed finegray(). Three adjustment models produced (data allow): Unadjusted - always included. Age sex adjusted - base = TRUE; age/sex must detectable standard UKB decoded names. Fully adjusted - covariates non-NULL.

title: Fine-Gray competing risks association analysis — assoc_competing
code: dt <- ops_toy(scenario = "association", n = 500) #> ✔ ops_toy: 500 participants | 33 columns | scenario = "association" | seed = 42 dt <- dt[dm_timing != 1L & htn_timing != 1L]  res <- assoc_competing(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p20116_i0",   compete_col  = "htn_status",   covariates   = c("bmi_cat", "tdi_cat") ) #> ℹ outcome_col dm_status: logical detected, converting TRUE/FALSE -> 1/0 #> ℹ outcome_col htn_status: logical detected, converting TRUE/FALSE -> 1/0 #> ℹ Mode B: dm_status (event) + htn_status (compete) #> ℹ Events: 22, Competing: 45, Censored: 317 #> ℹ Exposure: p20116_i0 #> ℹ   Model: Unadjusted #> ℹ   Model: Age and sex adjusted #> ℹ   Model: Fully adjusted #> ✔ Done: 6 result rows across 1 exposure and 3 models.

what: Cox proportional hazards association analysis — assoc_coxph
title: Cox proportional hazards association analysis — assoc_coxph
text: Fits one Cox models exposure variable returns tidy result table suitable downstream forest plots. default, two standard adjustment models always included alongside user-specified model:

title: Cox proportional hazards association analysis — assoc_coxph
code: assoc_coxph(   data,   outcome_col,   time_col,   exposure_col,   covariates = NULL,   base = TRUE,   strata = NULL,   test = c("wald", "lrt"),   cluster_col = NULL,   conf_level = 0.95 )  assoc_cox(   data,   outcome_col,   time_col,   exposure_col,   covariates = NULL,   base = TRUE,   strata = NULL,   test = c("wald", "lrt"),   cluster_col = NULL,   conf_level = 0.95 )

title: Cox proportional hazards association analysis — assoc_coxph
text: data (data.frame data.table) Analysis dataset. Must contain columns referenced outcome_col, time_col, exposure_col. outcome_col (character) Name event indicator column. Accepts logical (TRUE/FALSE) numeric/integer (0/1). time_col (character) Name follow-time column (numeric, consistent units, e.g. years). exposure_col (character) One exposure variable names. variable analysed separately; results stacked row-wise. covariates (character NULL) Additional covariate column names Fully adjusted model (e.g. c("tdi", "smoking", paste0("pc", 1:10))). NULL (default), Fully adjusted model run. base (logical) TRUE (default), always include Unadjusted Age sex adjusted models addition user-specified covariates model. Set FALSE run Fully adjusted model (requires covariates non-NULL). strata (character NULL) Optional stratification variable. Passed survival::strata() Cox formula. test (character) P-value method Cox models: "wald" (default) "lrt". cluster_col (character NULL) Optional clustering variable cluster-robust Cox variance, added model cluster(cluster_col). supplied, test must "wald". conf_level (numeric) Confidence level hazard ratio intervals. Default: 0.95.

title: Cox proportional hazards association analysis — assoc_coxph
text: data.table one row per exposure \(\times\) term \(\times\) model combination, following columns: exposure Exposure variable name. term Coefficient name returned coxph (e.g. "bmi_categoryObese" factor, variable name numeric/binary exposures). model Ordered factor: Unadjusted < Age sex adjusted < Fully adjusted. n Number participants included model (NA removal). n_events Number events model's analysis set (NA removal). person_years Total person-years follow-model's analysis set (rounded, NA removal). HR Hazard ratio (point estimate). CI_lower Lower bound confidence interval. CI_upper Upper bound confidence interval. p_value P-value method selected test. cluster_col supplied, cluster-robust Wald p-value. HR_label Formatted string, e.g. "1.23 (1.05-1.44)". returned table also carries hidden attribute recording outcome_col, time_col, covariates, exposure levels, strata, cluster_col, test, conf_level; audit_model reads automatically, nothing needs re-typed auditing result.

title: Cox proportional hazards association analysis — assoc_coxph
text: Unadjusted - covariates (crude). Age sex adjusted - age + sex auto-detected standard UKB names (p21022/p31) decoded names (age_at_recruitment/sex). Errors either column found. Fully adjusted - covariates supplied via covariates argument. run covariates non-NULL. Outcome coding: outcome_col may logical (TRUE/FALSE) integer/numeric (0/1). Logical values converted integer internally. Exposure types supported: Binary - 0/1 TRUE/FALSE; produces one term row per model. Factor - produces one term row per non-reference level. Numeric (continuous) - produces one term row per model. P-value method: test = "wald" returns term-level Wald p-value summary.coxph(). test = "lrt" returns exposure-level likelihood-ratio p-value single-term deletion (drop1(..., test = "Chisq")); factor exposures, overall exposure p-value repeated across non-reference level rows. cluster_col supplied, test = "wald" supported; Wald p-value confidence interval use cluster-robust variance summary.coxph().

title: Cox proportional hazards association analysis — assoc_coxph
code: dt <- ops_toy(scenario = "association", n = 500) #> ✔ ops_toy: 500 participants | 33 columns | scenario = "association" | seed = 42 dt <- dt[dm_timing != 1L]  res <- assoc_coxph(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p20116_i0",   covariates   = c("bmi_cat", "tdi_cat"),   base         = FALSE ) #> ℹ outcome_col dm_status: logical detected, converting TRUE/FALSE -> 1/0 #>  #> ── assoc_coxph ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ℹ 1 exposure x 1 model = 1 Cox regression #> ℹ Input cohort: 463 participants (n/n_events/person_years reflect each model's actual analysis set) #>  #> ── p20116_i0 ── #>  #> ✔   Fully adjusted | p20116_i0Previous: HR 0.39 (0.13-1.16), p = 0.0918 #> ✔   Fully adjusted | p20116_i0Current: HR 0.41 (0.09-1.77), p = 0.232 #> ✔ Done: 2 result rows across 1 exposure and 1 model.  # Fully adjusted only (skip Unadjusted + Age-sex) res <- assoc_coxph(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p20116_i0",   covariates   = c("p21022", "p31", "bmi_cat", "tdi_cat"),   base         = FALSE ) #> ℹ outcome_col dm_status: logical detected, converting TRUE/FALSE -> 1/0 #>  #> ── assoc_coxph ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ℹ 1 exposure x 1 model = 1 Cox regression #> ℹ Input cohort: 463 participants (n/n_events/person_years reflect each model's actual analysis set) #>  #> ── p20116_i0 ── #>  #> ✔   Fully adjusted | p20116_i0Previous: HR 0.41 (0.14-1.21), p = 0.105 #> ✔   Fully adjusted | p20116_i0Current: HR 0.42 (0.10-1.84), p = 0.253 #> ✔ Done: 2 result rows across 1 exposure and 1 model.

title: E-value for unmeasured confounding — assoc_evalue
text: Computes E-value (VanderWeele & Ding, 2017) one ratio effect estimates. E-value minimum strength association, risk ratio scale, unmeasured confounder need exposure outcome - measured covariates - fully explain away observed association. larger E-value means robust finding; benchmark strength measured confounders plausible unmeasured one.

Required manual mode; auto-detected result columns result mode. rare (logical NULL) Whether outcome rare (roughly < 15\ NULL (default) infers result's prevalence result mode; must supplied manual mode.

what: Restricted cubic spline dose-response analysis — assoc_rcs
title: Restricted cubic spline dose-response analysis — assoc_rcs
text: Models (possibly non-linear) dose-response relationship single continuous exposure outcome using restricted cubic splines (RCS), returns prediction curve - one row per grid point - rather single effect estimate. Whereas assoc_coxph friends assume linear (log-)effect assoc_trend handles ordered categorical exposures, assoc_rcs lets effect bend, capturing U-shaped, J-shaped, threshold, plateau relationships reporting test non-linearity.

title: Restricted cubic spline dose-response analysis — assoc_rcs
code: assoc_rcs(   data,   outcome_col,   time_col = NULL,   exposure_col,   method = c("coxph", "logistic", "linear"),   covariates = NULL,   base = TRUE,   knots = 4,   ref = NULL,   test = c("lrt", "wald"),   conf_level = 0.95,   np = 100 )

title: Restricted cubic spline dose-response analysis — assoc_rcs
text: data (data.frame data.table) Analysis dataset. outcome_col (character) Outcome column name. Event indicator (0/1 TRUE/FALSE) coxph/ logistic; continuous linear. time_col (character NULL) Follow-time column. Required method = "coxph". exposure_col (character) single continuous exposure column name. Factor logical exposures rejected - use assoc_trend assoc_coxph . method (character) Regression method: "coxph" (default), "logistic", "linear". covariates (character NULL) Covariates Fully adjusted model. Default: NULL. base (logical) Include Unadjusted Age--sex-adjusted models. Default: TRUE. knots (numeric) Number spline knots (single integer, typically 3, 4, 5) placed Harrell's recommended quantiles, explicit vector knot positions. Default: 4. ref (numeric NULL) Reference exposure value curve centred (effect equals 1 HR/scale, 0 linear). NULL (default) uses exposure median. test (character) P-value method: "lrt" (likelihood ratio, default) "wald". conf_level (numeric) Confidence level CI band. Default: 0.95. np (integer) Number points along prediction curve. Affects curve resolution , fitted model p-values. Default: 100.

title: Dose-response trend analysis — assoc_trend
code: assoc_trend(   data,   outcome_col,   time_col = NULL,   exposure_col,   method = c("coxph", "logistic", "linear"),   test = c("wald", "lrt"),   covariates = NULL,   base = TRUE,   scores = NULL,   conf_level = 0.95 )  assoc_tr(   data,   outcome_col,   time_col = NULL,   exposure_col,   method = c("coxph", "logistic", "linear"),   test = c("wald", "lrt"),   covariates = NULL,   base = TRUE,   scores = NULL,   conf_level = 0.95 )

title: Dose-response trend analysis — assoc_trend
text: data (data.frame data.table) Analysis dataset. outcome_col (character) Outcome column name. time_col (character NULL) Follow-time column (required method = "coxph"). exposure_col (character) One exposure column names. must factor (ordered unordered). first level used reference group. method (character) Regression method: "coxph" (default), "logistic", "linear". test (character) P-value method: "wald" (default) "lrt". covariates (character NULL) Covariates Fully adjusted model. Default: NULL. base (logical) Include Unadjusted Age--sex-adjusted models. Default: TRUE. scores (numeric NULL) Numeric scores assigned factor levels level order. Length must equal nlevels every exposure. NULL (default) uses 0, 1, 2, ... conf_level (numeric) Confidence level. Default: 0.95.

title: Dose-response trend analysis — assoc_trend
text: data.table one row per exposure \(\times\) level \(\times\) model, containing: exposure Exposure variable name. level Factor level (ordered factor preserving original level order). term Coefficient name returned model (reference row uses paste0(exposure, ref_level)). model Ordered factor: Unadjusted < Age sex adjusted < Fully adjusted. n Participants model (NA removal). ... Effect estimate columns categorical model: HR//beta, CI_lower, CI_upper, p_value, formatted label. Reference row HR = 1 / beta = 0 NA CI p. Cox models additionally include n_events person_years; logistic includes n_cases; linear includes se. HR_per_score / OR_per_score / beta_per_score Per-score-unit effect estimate trend model. Shared across levels within exposure \(\times\) model. HR_per_score_label / OR_per_score_label / beta_per_score_label Formatted string per-score estimate. p_trend P-value linear trend trend model. Shared across levels within exposure \(\times\) model. returned table also carries hidden attribute recording method, outcome_col, time_col, covariates, exposure levels, test, conf_level, plus exposure_scores: numeric trend score actually used per exposure, including auto-generated 0, 1, 2, ... scores scores NULL – otherwise recoverable result table . audit_model reads automatically.

title: Dose-response trend analysis — assoc_trend
text: Categorical model - exposure treated factor; produces one row per non-reference level (HR / / \(\beta\) vs reference). Trend model - exposure recoded numeric scores (default: 0, 1, 2, ...); produces per-score-unit effect estimate (*_per_score) p_trend. results merged: output contains reference row (effect = 1 / 0, CI = NA) followed non-reference rows, *_per_score p_trend appended shared columns (value within exposure \(\times\) model combination). Scores: default levels scored 0, 1, 2, ... reference group = 0 step = 1 unit. Supply scores use meaningful units (e.g. median years per category) - p_trend per-score estimate change; per-category HRs unaffected. Adjustment models: follows logic assoc_coxph - Unadjusted Age--sex-adjusted models included default (base = TRUE); Fully adjusted model added covariates non-NULL. P-value method: test controls categorical-model p_value trend-model p_trend. method = "linear", "lrt" uses conventional nested-model F test.

title: Dose-response trend analysis — assoc_trend
code: dt <- ops_toy(scenario = "association", n = 500) #> ✔ ops_toy: 500 participants | 33 columns | scenario = "association" | seed = 42 dt <- dt[dm_timing != 1L]  res <- assoc_trend(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "bmi_cat",   method       = "coxph",   covariates   = c("tdi_cat", "p20116_i0"),   base         = FALSE ) #> ! Exposure bmi_cat is not an ordered factor -- levels will be scored 0, 1, 2, ... (equal spacing assumed). #> ℹ outcome_col dm_status: logical detected, converting TRUE/FALSE -> 1/0 #>  #> ── assoc_trend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ℹ 1 exposure x 1 model (categorical + trend model per combination) | test: wald #>  #> ── bmi_cat ── #>  #> ℹ Levels: Underweight -> Normal -> Overweight -> Obese | Scores: 0, 1, 2, 3 #> ℹ   Fully adjusted | bmi_catUnderweight: 1.00 (ref) #> ✔   Fully adjusted | bmi_catNormal: HR 0.40 (0.10-1.64), p = 0.203 #> ✔   Fully adjusted | bmi_catOverweight: HR 0.40 (0.10-1.61), p = 0.196 #> ✔   Fully adjusted | bmi_catObese: HR 0.64 (0.17-2.43), p = 0.516 #> ℹ   Fully adjusted | trend: HR_per_score = 1.03 (0.66-1.60), p_trend = 0.893 #> ✔ Done: 4 result rows across 1 exposure and 1 model.

title: Derive a binary disease flag from UKB algorithmically-defined outcomes — derive_algorithm
text: {name}_alg_date Earliest algorithmically-defined event date (IDate).  Values coerced valid date, 1900-01-01 sentinel (see ), set NA. {name}_alg Logical flag derived {name}_alg_date: TRUE valid, non-sentinel date exists.  guarantees every positive case carries usable date time--event prevalent/incident classification. 1900-01-01 sentinel (derive_first_occurrence): per UKB ADO documentation (Resource 460, Algorithmically-defined outcomes v2.0), "Self-reported " case whose year onset missing (UKB field 20008) date set 1900-01-01.  Unlike true error code, parses valid date, .IDate alone silently admit real 1900 event.  derive_algorithm() therefore filters 1900-01-01 NA explicitly reports many rows affected.  Following package convention case must imply usable date, rows become non-cases ({name}_alg = FALSE).  Cases sourced HES death registries always carry real dates unaffected. self-contained case definition (route derive_case): ADO already reconciles self-report, HES, death internally, {name}_alg / {name}_alg_date final case definition.  Feed columns straight assoc_* (via outcome_col / time_col).  combine ADO separate derive_selfreport phenotype derive_case: double-counts self-report lets pmin pull date adjudication algorithm deliberately excluded. Unlike ICD-10 sources, ADO argument derive_icd10, matches ICD-10 codes. Column detection: source column located automatically field, handling raw format used extract_pheno snake_case format produced decode_names.  Supply col override auto-detection. data.table pass--reference: input data.table, new columns added -place via :=.

Every source-level rule-level intermediate result reported via cli (underlying derive_* calls, plus combined line per multi-rule source) discarded – nothing extra left data. keeps recipe's column footprint constant however many sources draws , matches naming derive_age, derive_timing, derive_followup already auto-detect ({name}_status / {name}_date), output plugs directly rest derive_* pipeline. Column auto-detection : recipe rule never records source column name, semantic definition (field, regex, icd10, icd9, opcs, read2, ctv3, histology, behaviour). Every dispatched derive_* call therefore relies function's auto-detection, matches raw UKB column names (p41270, participant.p41270) directly falls back extract_ls field dictionary data decode_names. override mechanism. required source column missing data (e.g. never extracted), underlying derive_* call aborts, exactly called directly – fall back status FALSE, downstream indistinguishable genuine "case". source whose column present matches codes different situation: warns contributes zero cases. data.table pass--reference: input data.table, two output columns added -place. title: Convert UKB imputed BGEN files to PGEN on RAP — grs_bgen2pgen
text: chr Integer vector. Chromosomes process. Default: 1:22. dest Character scalar. RAP destination path output PGEN files (e.g. "/pgen/"). Must specified explicitly. maf Numeric scalar. Minor allele frequency filter passed plink2 --maf. Variants MAF threshold excluded. Default: 0.01. Must (0, 0.5). instance Character scalar. Instance type preset: "standard" "large". See Details. Default: "standard". priority Character scalar. Job priority: "low" "high". Default: "low".

title: Convert UKB imputed BGEN files to PGEN on RAP — grs_bgen2pgen
text: character vector job IDs (one per chromosome), returned invisibly. Failed submissions NA. Use job_ls, job_status, job_wait monitor progress.

title: Convert UKB imputed BGEN files to PGEN on RAP — grs_bgen2pgen
text: function auto-generates plink2 driver script, uploads RAP project root (/) RAP, loops chr submitting one job per chromosome. 500 ms pause submissions prevents API rate-limiting. Output path critical. driver script writes plink2 output /home/dnanexus/// - fixed path Swiss Army Knife auto-uploads dest completion. Output files per chromosome: chr{N}_maf001.pgen/.pvar/.psam/.log. Instance types: "standard" mem2_ssd1_v2_x4: 4 cores, 12 GB RAM. Suitable smaller chromosomes (roughly chr 17-22). "large" mem2_ssd2_v2_x8: 8 cores, 28 GB RAM, 640 GB SSD. Required large chromosomes (roughly chr 1-16) standard storage insufficient. Must run inside RAP environment. Arguments validated first, bad chr maf reported wherever call ; environment check happens anything uploaded submitted.

title: Validate GRS predictive performance — grs_validate
