text: UK Biobank derives "algorithmically-defined outcome" (ADO, Category 42) 19 selected health outcomes across 8 disease groups (myocardial infarction, stroke, asthma, COPD, dementia, end-stage renal disease, motor neurone disease parkinsonism, several subtypes). outcome adjudication algorithm takes earliest recorded date across self-report, hospital inpatient death data, paired source field naming earliest record came . offline catalogue mapping outcome date source field IDs, right field can found without searching Showcase; date field feeds straight derive_algorithm.

"blood_count" 31 haematology measures category 100081 (field IDs 30000-30300 steps 10, instanced 0-2). what: First Occurrence health outcome fields (offline lookup) — ops_fo
title: First Occurrence health outcome fields (offline lookup) — ops_fo
text: UK Biobank derives "First Occurrence" field ~1,165 health outcomes defined 3-character ICD-10 level (chapters -XVII, excluding cancer chapter, covered cancer registry). outcome date field – earliest date condition recorded across self-report, primary care, hospital inpatient, death data – paired source field naming earliest record came . offline catalogue mapping outcome's ICD-10 code name date source field IDs, right field can found without searching Showcase; date field feeds straight derive_first_occurrence.

title: First Occurrence health outcome fields (offline lookup) — ops_fo
code: ops_fo(pattern = NULL, chapter = NULL)

title: First Occurrence health outcome fields (offline lookup) — ops_fo
text: pattern (character NULL) Optional case-insensitive keyword regular expression filtered across icd10 code, name, date_field / source_field IDs. code stem "I2" matches every code beginning I2 (I20-I29); field ID reverse lookup. Default NULL returns outcomes. chapter (character NULL) Optional case-insensitive keyword matched chapter column, e.g. "circulatory".

title: First Occurrence health outcome fields (offline lookup) — ops_fo
text: data.table columns: icd10 3-character ICD-10 code. name Outcome name. chapter ICD-10 chapter outcome belongs . date_field Integer field ID first-occurrence date. source_field Integer field ID paired source--report.

title: First Occurrence health outcome fields (offline lookup) — ops_fo
text: underlying code lists UK Biobank's algorithmic mapping clinically reviewed externally validated; treat First Occurrence outcome first pass identifying cases. full table always returned; pattern chapter subset . Console output reports came back – one line per chapter unfiltered call, single line otherwise.

what: Generate toy UKB-like data for testing and development — ops_toy

code: ops_toy(scenario = "cohort", n = 1000L, seed = 42L)

title: Generate toy UKB-like data for testing and development — ops_toy
text: scenario (character) Data structure generate: "cohort": wide participant-level table raw UKB field columns full derive_* -> assoc_* -> plot_* pipeline. "association": analysis-ready table covariates already factors, BMI/TDI binned, two pre-derived disease outcomes (dm_*, htn_*) including status, date, timing, follow-columns. Use assoc_* examples testing without running derive pipeline. "forest": association results table matching assoc_coxph() output, testing plot_forest(). n = number exposures (default 8). n (integer) Number participants – exposures "forest", participants matching cohort "gp", table returned many rows n. Default 1000L "cohort", 2000L "association", 8L "forest", 1000L "gp". seed (integer NULL) Random seed reproducibility. Pass NULL different dataset every call. Default 42L.

title: Generate toy UKB-like data for testing and development — ops_toy
text: data.table UKB-style column names. See Details columns included scenario.

title: Generate toy UKB-like data for testing and development — ops_toy
text: dataset entirely synthetic. Column names follow RAP conventions (e.g. p41270, p20002_i0_a0).

title: Generate toy UKB-like data for testing and development — ops_toy
text: Includes following column groups: Demographics: eid, p31, p34, p53_i0, p21022 Covariates: p21001_i0, p20116_i0, p1558_i0, p21000_i0, p22189, p54_i0 Genetic PCs: p22009_a1 - p22009_a10 Self-report disease: p20002_i0_a0-a4, p20008_i0_a0-a4 Self-report cancer: p20001_i0_a0-a4, p20006_i0_a0-a4 HES (position): p41270 (JSON array), p41280_a0-a8 HES ICD-9 (position): p41271 (JSON array), p41281_a0-a2 HES OPCS-4 (position): p41272 (JSON array), p41282_a0-a2 HES (main position): p41202 / p41262_a0-a8 (ICD-10), p41203 / p41263_a0-a2 (ICD-9), p41200 / p41260_a0-a2 (OPCS-4). generated subset matching -position field, derive_hes(position = "main") always returns subset derive_hes(position = ""). Cancer registry: p40006_i0-i2, p40011_i0-i2, p40012_i0-i2, p40005_i0-i2 Death registry: p40001_i0, p40002_i0_a0-a2, p40000_i0 Follow-censoring: p191 (date lost follow-) First occurrence: p131742 Algorithmic outcome: p42018 (dementia). Correlated HES self-report dementia records deliberately reducible : algorithm rejects code-positive participants admits code-negative ones, includes UKB's 1900-01-01 sentinel. GRS: grs_bmi, grs_raw, grs_finngen Messy columns: messy_allna, messy_empty, messy_label Disease codes sampled roughly equal frequency, event rates toy data run well real-world prevalence rare conditions rarer common ones. deliberate: realistic prevalence toy cohort hundred yields events assoc_* fit without unstable non-estimable coefficients. Use toy data check pipeline runs, never read anything effect sizes.

title: Generate toy UKB-like data for testing and development — ops_toy
text: Analysis-ready table. derive inputs (raw arrays, HES JSON, registry fields) omitted; derive outputs pre-computed internally consistent relationships: Demographics: eid, p31 (factor), p53_i0 (IDate), p21022 Covariates: p21001_i0, bmi_cat (factor, derived p21001_i0), p20116_i0 (factor), p1558_i0 (factor), p21000_i0 (factor), p22189, tdi_cat (factor, derived p22189 quartiles), p54_i0 (factor) Genetic PCs: p22009_a1 - p22009_a10 GRS: grs_bmi (continuous exposure) DM outcome: dm_status, dm_date, dm_timing, dm_followup_end, dm_followup_years (type 2 diabetes, ~12% prevalence) HTN outcome: htn_status, htn_date, htn_timing, htn_followup_end, htn_followup_years (hypertension, ~28% prevalence) Internal relationships guaranteed: bmi_cat cut p21001_i0 (breaks 18.5 / 25 / 30) tdi_cat cut p22189 quartiles dm_date NA iff dm_status = FALSE dm_timing: 0 = disease, 1 = prevalent, 2 = incident, NA = date dm_followup_years NA prevalent cases (dm_timing == 1)

title: Generate toy UKB-like data for testing and development — ops_toy
text: primary-care long table one row per clinical event, matching columns extract_gp(table = "gp_clinical") returns: eid, data_provider, read_2, read_3, event_dt. Pass gp argument derive_gp_read2(), derive_gp_ctv3() derive_recipe(). Unlike scenarios, n number participants matching cohort, number rows returned: roughly 45% linked primary-care data contributes several events, nrow() exceeds n. Use n seed "cohort" call joined , eid values line . data_provider decides code column row populates – England (TPP) records CTV3 read_3, providers record Read v2 read_2 – two coding systems never appear row. Event dates include UKB Coding 819 placeholders (1900-01-01 friends), count towards status excluded earliest-event date. Codes synthetic. Codes match shipped recipe taken recipe's code list derive_recipe() returns real cases; background codes fabricated correct shape curated code list.

title: Generate toy UKB-like data for testing and development — ops_toy
code: # cohort: raw UKB-style columns, feed into derive pipeline dt <- ops_toy(n = 100) #> ✔ ops_toy: 100 participants | 107 columns | scenario = "cohort" | seed = 42 dt <- derive_missing(dt) #> ✔ derive_missing: replaced 48 values across 3 columns (action = "na").  # association: analysis-ready, feed directly into assoc_* functions dt <- ops_toy(scenario = "association", n = 500) #> ✔ ops_toy: 500 participants | 33 columns | scenario = "association" | seed = 42 dt <- dt[dm_timing != 1L]   # exclude prevalent cases  # forest: results table for plot_forest() dt <- ops_toy(scenario = "forest") #> ✔ ops_toy: 24 rows | 11 columns | scenario = "forest" | seed = 42  # gp: primary-care long table, matched to a cohort by n and seed dt <- ops_toy(n = 200, seed = 1) #> ✔ ops_toy: 200 participants | 107 columns | scenario = "cohort" | seed = 1 gp <- ops_toy(scenario = "gp", n = 200, seed = 1) #> ✔ ops_toy: 83 linked participants | 952 records | 5 columns | scenario = "gp" | seed = 1 dt <- derive_gp_read2(dt, "t2d", read2 = c("C1041", "C10F6"), gp = gp) #> ✔ derive_gp_read2 (t2d): 2 cases, 2 with date.

title: Publication-ready forest plot — plot_forest
text: data data.frame. First column must label column (item). Additional columns displayed -(character) formatted named p_cols (must numeric). Column order preserved. May also assoc_*() result table (see Result-table shortcut). est Numeric vector. Point estimates (NA = CI drawn). NULL (default) = derive assoc_*() result data; required otherwise. lower Numeric vector. Lower CI bounds (length est). NULL (default) = derive assoc_*() result. upper Numeric vector. Upper CI bounds (length est). NULL (default) = derive assoc_*() result. ci_column Integer. Column position final rendered table gap/CI graphic placed. Must 2 ncol(data) + 1 (inclusive). NULL (default) = 2L, auto-placed result-table shortcut. ref_line Numeric. Reference line. NULL (default) = 1 (HR/), 0 beta coefficients result-table shortcut. xlim Numeric vector length 2. X-axis limits. NULL (default) uses c(0, 2), data-driven range result-table shortcut. ticks_at Numeric vector. Tick positions. NULL (default) = 5 evenly spaced ticks across xlim. arrow_lab Character vector length 2. Directional labels. Default: c("Lower risk", "Higher risk"). NULL = none. header Character vector length ncol(data) + 2. Column header labels final rendered table (original columns + gap_ci + label). NULL (default) = use column names data plus "gap_ci" "(95% CI)". Pass "" gap column position. label_col Character. Result-table shortcut : result column becomes row label. NULL (default) = "model" single-exposure table, otherwise "term". Ignored base path. show_cols Character vector. Result-table shortcut : result columns display alongside label (besides auto CI graphic). NULL (default) = primary count column (n_events/n_cases/n) plus p_value. Ignored base path. indent Integer vector (length = nrow(data)). Indentation level label column: unit adds two leading spaces. Default: zeros. bold_label Logical vector (length = nrow(data)). rows bold label column. NULL (default) = auto-derive indent: rows indent == 0 bolded (parent rows), indented sub-rows plain. ci_col Character scalar vector (length = nrow(data)). CI colour(s). NA rows skipped automatically. Default: "black". ci_sizes Numeric. Point size. Default: 0.6. ci_Theight Numeric. CI cap height. Default: 0.2. ci_digits Integer. Decimal places auto-generated (95% CI) column. Default: 2L. ci_sep Character. Separator lower upper CI label, e.g. ", " " - ". Default: ", ". p_cols Character vector. Names numeric p-value columns data. formatted p_digits decimal places "<0.001"-style clipping. NULL = none. p_digits Integer. Decimal places p-value formatting. Default: 3L. bold_p TRUE (bold non-NA p p_threshold), FALSE (bolding), logical vector (per-row control). Default: TRUE. p_threshold Numeric. P-value threshold bolding bold_p = TRUE. Default: 0.05. align Integer vector length ncol(data) + 2. Alignment per column: -1 left, 0 centre, 1 right. Must cover final columns (original + gap_ci + label). NULL = auto (column 1 left, others centre). background Character. Row background style: "zebra", "bold_label" (shade rows bold_label = TRUE), "none". Default: "zebra". bg_col Character. Shading colour backgrounds (scalar), per-row vector length nrow(data) (overrides style). Default: "#F0F0F0". border Character. Border style: "three_line" "none". Default: "three_line". border_width Numeric. Border line width(s). Scalar = three lines width; length-3 vector = top--header, bottom--header, bottom--body. Default: 3. row_height NULL (auto), numeric scalar, numeric vector (length = total gtable rows including margins). Auto sets 8 / 12 / 10 / 15 mm top / header / data / bottom respectively. col_width NULL (auto), numeric scalar, numeric vector (length = total gtable columns). Auto rounds default width adjustment \([5, 10)\) mm. save Logical. Save output files? Default: FALSE. dest Character. Destination file path (extension ignored; four formats saved). Required save = TRUE. save_width Numeric. Output width cm. Default: 20. save_height Numeric NULL. Output height cm. NULL = nrow(data) * 0.9 + 3. theme Character preset ("default") forestploter::forest_theme object. Default: "default".

title: Publication-ready forest plot — plot_forest
code: # --- Result-table shortcut: pass an assoc_*() result straight in ---------- dt  <- ops_toy(scenario = "association", n = 500) #> ✔ ops_toy: 500 participants | 33 columns | scenario = "association" | seed = 42 dt  <- dt[dm_timing != 1L] res <- assoc_coxph(   data         = dt,   outcome_col  = "dm_status",   time_col     = "dm_followup_years",   exposure_col = "p20116_i0",   covariates   = c("bmi_cat", "tdi_cat") ) #> ℹ outcome_col dm_status: logical detected, converting TRUE/FALSE -> 1/0 #>  #> ── assoc_coxph ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ℹ 1 exposure x 3 models = 3 Cox regressions #> ℹ Input cohort: 463 participants (n/n_events/person_years reflect each model's actual analysis set) #>  #> ── p20116_i0 ── #>  #> ✔   Unadjusted | p20116_i0Previous: HR 0.39 (0.13-1.16), p = 0.0905 #> ✔   Unadjusted | p20116_i0Current: HR 0.41 (0.10-1.77), p = 0.233 #> ✔   Age and sex adjusted | p20116_i0Previous: HR 0.40 (0.14-1.20), p = 0.102 #> ✔   Age and sex adjusted | p20116_i0Current: HR 0.43 (0.10-1.85), p = 0.255 #> ✔   Fully adjusted | p20116_i0Previous: HR 0.39 (0.13-1.16), p = 0.0918 #> ✔   Fully adjusted | p20116_i0Current: HR 0.41 (0.09-1.77), p = 0.232 #> ✔ Done: 6 result rows across 1 exposure and 3 models. plot(plot_forest(res))   # est/CI/ref/columns all auto-derived #> ✔ plot_forest: detected HR result: 6 rows, reference line at 1.   # --- Base path: full manual control --------------------------------------- df <- data.frame(   item      = c("Exposure vs. control", "Unadjusted", "Fully adjusted"),   `Cases/N` = c("", "89/4521", "89/4521"),   p_value   = c(NA_real_, 0.001, 0.006),   check.names = FALSE )  p <- plot_forest(   data       = df,   est        = c(NA, 1.52, 1.43),   lower      = c(NA, 1.18, 1.11),   upper      = c(NA, 1.96, 1.85),   ci_column  = 2L,   indent     = c(0L, 1L, 1L),   bold_label = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE),   p_cols     = "p_value",   xlim       = c(0.5, 3.0) ) plot(p)

title: Build a phenotype recipe — recipe_new
text: id (character) Recipe id; globally unique, key recipe_get matches . Identifies one definition. label (character) Human-readable phenotype name. Two recipes operationalise phenotype differently share label told apart id. sources (list) Named list source slots; see Details. Slot names must come eleven documented recipe_get. short_label (character) Optional short name phenotype. version (numeric) Whole number; bump every change. Default 1. created, updated (Date "YYYY-MM-DD") Authoring dates. Default today, updated following created. description (character) Optional free-text summary definition. logic (list) Optional list(case=, date=); case ""/"" date "earliest"/"latest". Defaults case = "", date = "earliest". notes (character) Caveats, one per element. Provenance part definition derive_* execute belong – notes channel recipe object, print, catalogue can see.

title: Build a phenotype recipe — recipe_new

title: Build a phenotype recipe — recipe_new
text: recipe_new builds validates definition; add bundled library decide whether definition appropriate study. contributed recipe reviewed becomes part library – see contributing guide. element sources may given : bare vector – shorthand slot's code field, e.g. hes = c("I21", "I22") (available selfreport, whose rule also needs field); single recipe_rule, modifiers match cause needed; list recipe_rules, slot whose rules differ one another – cancer-registry histology/behaviour branches usual case. Omitted slots recorded unused. Rule fields absent left rather written nulls: empty histology filter absent one mean thing derive_*.

code: recipe_new(   id     = "myocardial_infarction_demo",   label  = "Myocardial infarction",   sources = list(     hes   = recipe_rule(icd10 = c("I21", "I22"), match = "prefix"),     death = recipe_rule(icd10 = c("I21", "I22"), match = "prefix",                         cause = "primary")   ),   notes = "Provenance: worked example, not a published definition." ) #> ✔ recipe_new: "myocardial_infarction_demo" - 2 rules across 2 sources. #>  #> ── Recipe: Myocardial infarction ─────────────────────────────────────────────── #> id: myocardial_infarction_demo | version 1 | updated 2026-08-21 #>  #> Sources #>   • hes  icd10="I21,I22"  match="prefix" #>   • death  icd10="I21,I22"  match="prefix"  cause="primary" #>  #> Logic case=any | date=earliest #>  #> Notes #>   1. what: ukbflow: Streamlined Workflow for UK Biobank Data Extraction, Analysis, and Visualization — ukbflow-package
title: ukbflow: Streamlined Workflow for UK Biobank Data Extraction, Analysis, and Visualization — ukbflow-package
text: Provides R-native, RAP-aware workflow system UK Biobank controlled-data analysis Research Analysis Platform (RAP). Includes tools phenotype extraction decoding, variable derivation, survival association analysis, genetic risk score computation, audit records, publication-quality visualization. details UK Biobank resource, see Bycroft et al. (2018) doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0579-z .
